elements.evidence: "the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim by the Company to HDI under this Agreement"

elements.element: Cap limb (b): USD 1,000,000 floor, expressed as greater-of
elements.evidence: "shall not exceed the greater of (a) ... and (b) USD 1,000,000"

elements.element: Cap is mutual (applies to each Party)
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed"
"neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect or consequential damages"

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes
elements.evidence: "Customer's payment obligations, being all amounts due from the Company under this Agreement, are not \"damages\" for purposes of this Section 10.9"
"each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"

reasons: The Agreement contained no limitation of liability provision; a single concise inserted section 10.9 is an appropriate minimal cure and no existing sentence was rewritten or disturbed.

All preferred atomic elements are present in operative language: greater-of cap with the exact fee basis ("paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim") and the USD 1,000,000 floor, mutuality ("each Party's total aggregate liability"), mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, and the full uncapped carve-out set (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, other party's IP infringement).
The payment-obligations savings clause is express and correctly anchored to the cap section.

Minor drafting note only: the insertion uses the label "Customer's", which is not a defined alias in this HDI/Company agreement, but the apposition "being all amounts due from the Company under this Agreement" resolves the reference, so no dangling term or contradiction is introduced.
Result: compliant at the preferred position; no further redline needed.
